responses.global_local: Across the 1,733 evaluation requests, bureau_score was the most important feature: shuffling it lowered Average Precision by 0.127 across three runs. In the 300-request SHAP sample, it also had the highest average SHAP value (0.904 log-odds), followed by dti (0.544). For TR-009585, the biggest positive contributions were bureau_score (+2.27), dti (+1.20), and loan_amount_sar (+0.20). The global results describe the model overall; the local results explain just this one request.
responses.output_units: SHAP values are in log-odds (raw margin), not probability points: raw margin = base value + sum of SHAP values. Calibration then adjusts that probability: for TR-009585, 0.9031 raw became 0.4795 calibrated.The background is the training tree-path distribution, and sigmoid(base_value) is not necessarily the mean predicted probability. The additivity error was very small (5.7e-15).
responses.reason_limits: The three reason statements show which features pushed the model’s score up for this request. They do not explain why someone would default, and changing a feature does not guarantee a different result. Related features can share information, so their individual importance may look smaller. Changing bureau_score by one point did not change this request’s top three reasons, but that is only a small check on one request.
responses.calibration_evidence: On the evaluation set (1,733 requests, 139 defaults), calibration improved the Brier score from 0.1130 to 0.0671, ECE from 0.1469 to 0.0225, and log loss from 0.358 to 0.247. ROC-AUC stayed at 0.7708 and Average Precision stayed at 0.2587 because calibration kept the ranking the same. ECE also went down in Q3 (0.134 to 0.032 across 836 requests) and Q4 (0.159 to 0.024 across 897 requests). ECE depends on how probability ranges are grouped, so results from groups with few requests should be treated carefully.
responses.stability: The paired customer-cluster bootstrap gives a 95% percentile interval for AP of 0.197 to 0.338 and for Brier change of -0.054 to -0.037, so the improvement is consistently negative. The interval holds the model and calibrator fixed, so it excludes training uncertainty, calibration-fitting uncertainty and future drift. It is not a confidence interval for any one applicant's probability, and the two quarters are not independent folds.
responses.review_capacity: The threshold was selected on the policy set using the 10×FN+FP loss and a 12% capacity limit. It flagged 68 of 589 requests, within the limit of 70. The raw threshold was 0.588 and the calibrated threshold was 0.173. On evaluation, the combined review group exceeded capacity in both quarters: 109 of 836 requests in Q3 (limit 100) and 122 of 897 in Q4 (limit 107). Risk flags alone were already over capacity in Q4 (109). The result is CAPACITY_REVIEW_REQUIRED, so I did not retune the threshold on evaluation data.
